chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Salim informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Walid (meaning al-Basri) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far (meaning Ghandar) narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sammak ibn Harb, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Samurah saying: I heard the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) saying:
There will be after me twelve leaders. And he said a word that I did not hear. The people said: He said: They are all from Quraysh.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the twelve leaders after him?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, establishes the foundational Shia belief in the twelve divinely appointed successors (Imams) from the Quraysh, mirroring the well-known Sunni narration of 'twelve caliphs' but emphasizing their spiritual authority. The specific mention of 'Amir' (commander/leader) underscores their political and religious leadership, while the tribal constraint highlights the Prophet's emphasis on Qurayshi lineage for these successors. This text serves as a critical scriptural proof for the Imamate of the Twelve Imams, linking their succession directly to the Prophet's explicit prophecy.
